item.title: Iran says U.S. election results show Americans reject the war
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday that the U.S. midterm election results reflected Americans' rejection of the war President Trump launched against his country. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf added a warning that if Mr. Trump does not heed the message from American voters, it will bring "a Nightmare."President Trump acknowledged Tuesday night that the war with Iran was partially to blame for the GOP's resounding midterm elections losses. But Mr. Trump told The Wall Street Journal he didn't regret the conflict and added he "would have done it again."Despite signs of a diplomatic push to reach a peace deal, ships continue to come under attack in the Strait of Hormuz. Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while transiting the waterway, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Wednesday.
New Updates
1m ago
Iranians take to streets of Tehran for pro-regime rally
People marched through central Tehran Wednesday in a major pro-regime rally to mark the 47th anniversary of the 1979 takeover of the U.S. embassy in the Iranian capital, chanting anti-U.S. and Israel slogans.
Some held signs calling for revenge for the killing of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the outset of the ongoing war, while others mocked President Trump.
"We are not happy about the surge in oil prices," said one woman, who gave AFP only her last name, Mahmoudkhani.
"But there is some satisfaction in knowing we are no longer living this torment alone. We, alone, have been suffering under sanctions for so many years," she added.

item.title: Iran dismisses U.S. response to peace proposal
item.description:
Follow updates on the war in the Middle East for Wednesday, November 4, here. See earlier developments below.
What to know about the Iran war: A senior Iranian figure on Tuesday cast doubt on diplomatic efforts to broker a peace deal with the U.S., calling the Trump administration's response to the latest proposal "not convincing" and insisting that Iran's demands, including for a halt to fighting on all fronts in the Middle East, must be met if the Strait of Hormuz is to reopen.American forces launched limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets near the strait on Monday, multiple U.S. officials told CBS News, in response to an apparent Iranian attack targeting a U.S. aircraft. President Trump said on the eve of U.S. midterm elections that a deal with Iran to end the eight-month war still "could happen," insisting Tehran "wants a settlement, as soon as possible."
New Updates
4:44 PM / November 3, 2026
Tanker hit by 2 projectiles off northeast coast of Oman, U.K. maritime agency says
Two unknown projectiles struck a tanker traveling near the northeast coast of Oman on Tuesday, according to a U.K. maritime agency.
The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations said it received a report from the tanker's security officer, who said the projectiles hit the vessel's engine room. It's not known who was operating the tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, where it came from or where it was headed.
No injuries or environmental impact had been reported, according to UKMTO.

item.title: U.S. launches strikes on Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
The U.S. military launched limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, multiple U.S. officials told CBS News.
The strikes targeted Iran's Qeshm Island, a senior U.S. official said. It came after two incidents on Monday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards fired at an American fighter jet, leading it to return fire, according to two U.S. military officials. Later Monday, Iran fired a missile from Qeshm Island that threatened shipping, the officials said.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the strikes, which came on the eve of Election Day in the U.S. President Trump has been floating the idea of restarting hostilities with Iran after the midterms, at the same time as U.S. and Qatari mediators broker talks on a possible U.S.-Iran deal.
Qeshm Island, in the northern Strait of Hormuz, is crucial to the Iranian regime's efforts to monitor and exert control over commercial traffic through the waterway.
Map shows the location of Qeshm Island, off the coast of Iran in the northern Strait of Hormuz.
Omar Zaghloul/Anadolu via Getty Images
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tuesday that Tehran retained "the right to legitimate self-defense" after the new U.S. strikes, and would do so "until the military aggression has been completely and permanently brought to an end."
Iran has retaliated for attacks on its territory throughout the war sparked by joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Feb. 28 by targeting commercial shipping traffic in the strait and U.S. allies and interests across the Persian Gulf region.

item.title: Poland launches major security operation along border with Russia
item.description:
Berlin — Poland launched a large-scale security operation this week along its border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, the country's national police chief said, and the Polish prime minister said the effort may have prevented a sabotage or provocation operation targeting the NATO member.
Additional police and counterterrorism units, as well as troops from the elite military special forces unit GROM, have been deployed as part of the operation, which national police chief Marek Boroń said would run from Monday until at least Nov. 8.
Polish and allied intelligence agencies had warned of possible sabotage operations and provocations during the first half of November, particularly along Poland's border with Kaliningrad, and including possible border incursions by armed groups.
Those warnings had already put domestic security agencies on high alert even before the additional security forces were deployed to the northeast regions of Warmia-Masuria and Podlaskie.
Tourists stand next to a razor-wire fence along the Polish-Lithuanian border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, near the village of Grzybina, in Poland's Podlaskie province, near the Suwalki Gap, Sept. 26, 2026.
Sergei GAPON/AFP/Getty
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday that suspicious movements were observed overnight near Kaliningrad, including individuals carrying flashlights close to the border area.
He said the quick reaction by Polish security forces may have prevented an unspecified provocation this week.
"We very quickly mobilized the necessary security forces and means on site, and we successfully prevented any attempted acts of provocation, if that was the intention. Of course, we will never be able to completely confirm that," Tusk said Tuesday, addi...

item.title: 5 people rescued in South Pacific after months at sea, 4 still missing
item.description:
Five people, including two children, were rescued this week in the South Pacific island nation of Kiribati after three months drifting at sea in a 20-foot skiff, authorities said. Another four remained missing.
Villagers rescued the group Sunday off Fanning Island in Kiribati, the Australian Broadcasting Corp. reported, after they had drifted an estimated 3,355 miles east from the Federated States of Micronesia.
The U.S. Coast Guard in Guam on Tuesday confirmed that the skiff with nine people aboard had been reported missing after it failed to return to Ruo Island in Micronesia on July 30. The group had been making a one-hour crossing between the islands of Murilo and Ruo at the time, ABC reported.
A 10-day search covering 33,000 square miles followed without any sign of the missing boat or those aboard, it said.
"Incredible and wonderful news these five folks were found and are receiving care," the U.S. Coast Guard told The Associated Press in an email.
"Our profound condolences to family and friends of those who did not arrive with them," the email added.
Fanning Island.
Gail Shotlander / Getty Images
When asked by the AP what happened to the missing four, the U.S. Coast Guard said it was continuing to gather and confirm information and would reply as soon as possible.
A lawmaker in Kiribati, Kaotitaake Rakoroa, told ABC the survivors were being cared for by a pastor on the island.
Nursing officer Paukin Tororo told the ABC on Monday that all five were severely dehydrated and malnourished. They were put on intravenous drips and were showing signs of recovery.
"They can give a smile face, they show the sign they want to eat," she told the ABC.
The survivors had yet to speak publicly about their ordeal and had reques...

item.title: 1 dead, 2 injured in helicopter crash near Mount Everest base camp
item.description:
Two helicopters collided Tuesday while trying to land just below Mount Everest's base camp, killing at least one person and injuring two others, officials said.
The aircraft were ferrying trekkers who had been hiking up to Everest base camp during Nepal's popular trekking season. Heavy snow had covered the route before the weather improved Sunday and thousands of trekkers were able to move around.
There are no roads on Everest, and helicopters are the only way to bring down trekkers and guides who become sick or exhausted in the cold and high altitude.
The helicopters crashed at Pheriche village, which is at an altitude of 13,780 feet.
A 47-year-old tourist from India was killed in the crash, according to Bhupendra Thapa, a Solukhumbhu district administration officer. Arrangements were being made to airlift the tourist's remains to Kathmandu, the Agence France-Presse reported.
The location of a helicopter collision on Nepal's Mount Everest.
Elif Acar/Anadolu via Getty Images
A passenger from New Zealand was injured and was being transported to the capital, Kathmandu, for treatment. A Nepali pilot sustained injuries but was treated locally.
The number of people on the two helicopters wasn't clear.
The Mount Everest base camp trek lasts up to two weeks and goes from the only airstrip in the area at Lukla to base camp located at 17,380 feet. Everest's summit is at an altitude of over 29,000 feet. The trek is popular during the fall season, right after the rainy season and before the harsh winter months.

item.title: Soccer player dies following on-field collision in Spain
item.description:
A Spanish soccer player's death is now under investigation as possible involuntary manslaughter, after he suffered a fatal injury in an on-field collision during a match.
The country's National Police said Tuesday that proceedings were opened and prosecutors will also be involved.
Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died after he suffered cardiac arrest from the on-field collision in a Spanish second-division match, his club said. He was 30 years old.
De Miguel was challenging for the ball near midfield on Monday when he was struck in the chest by the onrushing Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during added time.
Owono was shown a straight red card for the incident.
De Miguel was taken to a hospital and the match, tied 2-2, was abandoned after the incident.
Tenerife said in a statement to Spanish media late Monday that De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest but that his pulse was restored in the ambulance to the hospital. However, it later said his condition had "worsened neurologically" and subsequently announced that De Miguel had died at 8 a.m.
The club, located on Spain's Canary Islands, said it was "heartbroken."
"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness," the club wrote, in part, in a statement announcing the death on social media. "The family of Jesús de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments."
De Miguel, a Madrid native, made his professional debut in 2015 with Leganés B and has since played for a number of lower-divisions clubs in Spain. He joined Tenerife last year.
"There are no words of comfort," the club statement read. "There is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community."

item.title: Stolen watch worth $290,000 returned to store with apology note
item.description:
A Swiss luxury watch worth about $290,000 that was stolen from a Tokyo store last week has been returned with an apology note, according to local media.
The theft occurred when a man posing as a customer tried on the Audemars Piguet timepiece and then fled the shop in the Japanese capital while it was still on his wrist.
But the case took a twist when the store received a package containing the watch -- and a handwritten note saying sorry, the Asahi Shimbun newspaper and other media reported on Monday, citing unnamed investigative sources.
The watch's serial number reportedly identified it as the stolen item.
A name and address were also written on the package, but police believe the information is fake, the Japan Times reported.
The shop declined to comment when contacted by AFP.
Tokyo police are still searching for the man on suspicion of theft, according to the Asahi Shumbun.
In August, four luxury watches worth 200 million yen ($1.3 million) were stolen from another store in the same shopping complex. Two Chilean nationals were arrested on suspicion of theft in connection with the incident and subsequently indicted, the Japan Times reported.
A man gestures as he speaks with a Japanese television reporter in an alley outside Nakano Broadway, reportedly used by the suspects to flee following a robbery at the Time Walker luxury watch store, in Tokyo's Nakano district, Japan, August 25, 2026.
David Mareuil/Anadolu via Getty Images
After that robbery, police conducted a crime prevention session for watch store owners, advising that they only display replicas, the Asahi Simbun reported. They were also taught how to use a special lining on display cases to make them difficult to break.
